commentary_segments.text: The output stage is easily recognized because of the cross-coupled quad. It is preceded by a double folded cascode. No g equalization m is used. The points of high impedance are labeled by big (red) dots. This is clearly a two-stage amplifier. Point A is one input of the output stage. Point B is now the other one; it is no longer connected to ground. It is derived from point A by an inverter (with transistors M25-M26) which is loaded by the 1/g ’s of the two transistors M27 and M28. Its gain is thus about minus unity. m The output stage now has a differential drive. The output stage presents a load to the input stage of about 15 pF (at point A). This capacitor determines the GBW.
